article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Zkittlez × Do-Si-Dos
Breeder: Archive Seed Bank / The Docta
THC Content: 24–30%
CBD Content: Typically very low
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , limonene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Berry candy, lime, tropical fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Moonbow arrived at exactly the point when modern cannabis breeding was learning how to combine extreme candy terpenes with the deeper potency and structure of OG-influenced genetics. Archive Seed Bank took Zkittlez, famous for its almost artificial fruit-candy intensity, and paired it with Do-Si-Dos, a resinous Cookies-and-OG descendant created within Archive’s own breeding program. The result became much more than another sweet hybrid. Beneath the berry and citrus candy sits an earthy, gassy Kush backbone, while the experience can move from bright euphoria into a remarkably comfortable body state. Certain selections became especially famous, including Moonbow #75 and the award-winning #112, both of which went on to influence an expanding family of high-profile marijuana genetics.
Genetics and Lineage

The pedigree is straightforward at the first generation: Zkittlez × Do-Si-Dos. The Zkittlez parent is The Original Z and traces Do-Si-Dos through OGKB and Archive’s Face Off OG BX1. That makes Moonbow a meeting point between two major branches of modern American weed breeding. Zkittlez contributes intensely saturated fruit and candy aroma, while Do-Si-Dos brings Cookies influence, OG structure, resin and a heavier earthy-gas component.

What happened after the original cross is equally important. Archive hunted large populations for exceptional phenotypes, and selections such as #75 and #112 became breeding parents in their own right. Moonbow #75 helped create Rainbow Belts when crossed back to Zkittlez, while #112 became the focus of a multi-year stabilization project. Archive eventually produced Moonbow 112 IX by combining #112 F1 with a selected #112 F2 plant rather than simply cloning or backcrossing the original. The genetic influence of the original Moonbow consequently extends far beyond a single cultivar.
Effects and Experience

The first portion of the high can be deceptively lively. Moonbow often produces a noticeable cerebral lift, with mood becoming brighter and ordinary sensory experiences gaining greater intensity. Conversation, music and creative activities can feel more immersive, while the Zkittlez side contributes a playful quality that keeps the initial experience from feeling overly heavy. Current consumer data places relaxed, happy and euphoric among its most frequently selected effects, illustrating the strain’s blend of mental pleasure and calm.

Physical relaxation usually becomes clearer as the session develops. Rather than dropping immediately into sedation, the cultivar can gradually trade its energetic edge for a warmer body sensation and quieter mental rhythm. That progression is one reason Moonbow can feel balanced despite considerable potency. Contemporary examples can test well into the upper-20% range. Consumers with limited tolerance should therefore allow the first dose to develop fully before increasing intake. High-THC cannabis can substantially alter mood, thinking and perception, and NIDA notes that some people experience anxiety, fear or panic rather than relaxation.
Medical Benefits

The combination of euphoria and later physical calm may interest medical marijuana consumers seeking an evening or late-day cultivar. Some people use THC-rich cannabis when dealing with persistent discomfort, poor appetite, low mood or difficulty settling down, while Moonbow’s strong psychoactive character may be preferable for experienced patients who find lower-potency flower insufficient. Those possibilities should not be confused with evidence that this particular strain treats pain, anxiety, depression or insomnia. Its chemical composition can differ significantly from one producer and phenotype to another.

Broader research on medical cannabis provides more cautious context. A systematic review of randomized trials found that non-inhaled medical cannabis and cannabinoids produced small improvements in pain relief and sleep quality among some chronic-pain patients, while also increasing adverse effects such as dizziness and drowsiness. Those findings involve standardized cannabinoid products rather than Moonbow flower specifically. Anyone using weed alongside prescription medication or attempting to manage a significant health condition should discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Moonbow’s reputation was built largely on aroma. Zkittlez supplies vivid fruit-candy sweetness, but Do-Si-Dos prevents the profile from becoming one-dimensional. Archive describes the celebrated #112 expression as dripping with blackberry, currant and zingy lime Zkittlez terpenes, while related Archive material adds skunky Kush, petrol, earth and darker OG-style funk. The resulting flower can smell like crushed berry candy and citrus peel at first, then reveal grape, damp earth, dough, spice and fuel as the buds are broken apart.

Published terpene descriptions commonly emphasize caryophyllene and limonene, with linalool and occasionally ocimene appearing in broader profiles. Caryophyllene complements the peppery, Kush-like base, while limonene fits the bright lime and citrus qualities; linalool can reinforce the softer floral side. Laboratory chemistry varies between Moonbow phenotypes, however, so those compounds should be treated as a common framework rather than a guaranteed percentage breakdown. Archive itself places greater emphasis on the cultivar’s blackberry-currant-lime candy expression than on a fixed laboratory terpene formula.
Growing Information

Moonbow tends to reward growers who have enough vertical room to let the plant express itself. Archive’s description of Moonbow #112 IX—the line developed to recreate the original #112 selection—emphasizes tall, well-structured plants producing grenade-sized flowers along colas that can approach a foot in length. Resin production is substantial, with Archive describing most phenotypes as exceptionally sticky. Original Moonbow cultivation figures were never standardized into a simple breeder yield chart, so precise grams-per-square-meter claims should be treated cautiously.

A realistic indoor flowering period is roughly nine to ten weeks. Archive-derived Moonbow #112 IX is documented at approximately 67 days, placing it squarely within that window. Outdoors, plants generally require enough season to mature around October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Strong branching responds well to canopy management, and taller phenotypes can benefit from topping or training when vertical space is limited.

Flower quality rather than raw tonnage has always been central to Archive’s Moonbow work. The breeder explicitly states that Moonbow 112 IX was selected with flower quality first, even though some phenotypes also perform respectably for solventless extraction. Dense, resinous buds demand reliable airflow and controlled humidity late in bloom, while strong terpene production makes odor management important indoors. Overall difficulty is moderate: the plant is vigorous enough to be manageable, but maximizing its resin, aroma and structure requires more attention than a basic beginner cultivar.
FAQ
Is Moonbow indica or sativa?

Moonbow is best described as a balanced hybrid rather than forcing it into a strict indica or sativa category. Archive-related databases classify it broadly as indica/sativa, and its effects combine an upbeat cerebral beginning with progressively stronger physical relaxation.
What are the genetics of Moonbow?
Archive Seed Bank created Moonbow by crossing Zkittlez with Do-Si-Dos. Archive’s current Moonbow #112 material explicitly identifies the original #112 as an F1 selection of Zkittlez × Do-Si-Dos.
How strong is Moonbow?

Potency varies considerably by grower and phenotype. User reports currently list Moonbow at approximately 30% THC, while other commercial and strain-reference examples commonly fall somewhere in the mid-to-upper 20% range. Laboratory results from the specific flower are more meaningful than a universal strain percentage.
What does Moonbow taste like?

Expect fruit candy layered with darker Kush character. Blackberry, currant, lime, grape and tropical sweetness can appear alongside earth, floral notes, skunk and gas. Archive’s #112 selection is particularly associated with blackberry-currant and zingy lime Zkittlez terpenes.
How long does Moonbow take to flower?

Approximately nine to ten weeks is a reasonable indoor expectation. Archive’s later Moonbow #112 IX, created specifically to recreate the original #112 F1 selection, is documented at roughly 67 days of flowering.
Final Thoughts on Moonbow

Moonbow occupies an important place in modern cannabis because it solved a breeding problem that has challenged many Zkittlez hybrids: preserving explosive candy flavor while adding better structure, potency and depth. Archive Seed Bank’s combination of Zkittlez and Do-Si-Dos brought blackberry, lime and fruit-candy terpenes together with OG-influenced gas, earth and resin, creating marijuana that is recognizable from both aroma and effect.

Its importance only grew as Archive selected exceptional plants from the original population. Moonbow #75 became part of Rainbow Belts, while #112 developed into an award-winning selection and ultimately inspired the Moonbow 112 IX preservation project. For consumers, the cultivar offers high potency, unusual candy-and-Kush flavor and an experience that moves from euphoria toward calm. For growers and breeders, its lasting value lies in something broader: Moonbow became a genetic platform from which an entire generation of premium Z-influenced cannabis could be built.
